thread:
olivia: FYI launching an optional monthly spend cap feature for hosted accounts next billing cycle (effective 2026-09-01). Customers can enable a hard or soft cap at account level.

marco: Quick clarification: hard = auto-pause, soft = warn + grace credit?

olivia: Exactly. Hard caps will auto-pause API keys when the billing spend reaches the cap. Soft caps will allow traffic for up to a 48-hour grace window and then apply a one-time grace credit up to $50 if the customer requests review.

amy: Does enabling a cap affect our rate-limit behavior? We need to be clear.

olivia: No change to runtime limits. Caps operate in billing plane only. Requests exceeding rate limits still get throttled normally. Caps just stop new billing-eligible tokens by pausing keys.

billing-bot: Example notification flow:
- 90% cap reached: send email + platform banner
- 100% soft cap: allow 48h then flag for review
- 100% hard cap: auto-pause key immediately and create billing hold

support: We'll add macros: "Your account hit a billing cap; explain options to lift or request a grace review."

sales-lead: Can partners/resellers set caps on behalf of customers?

olivia: Yes, partner-admins can set caps for their subaccounts. For enterprise committed deals, caps are disabled by default but can be negotiated.

marco: Any invoice or line-item changes?

olivia: Invoices will include a new line: "Monthly spend cap status: <enabled|soft|hard>" and any applied grace credit will show as a separate adjustment. Finance will run a weekly report of capped accounts.

support: We'll prep a KB and add the toggle to the billing UI beta toggle. Expect +ticket volume after launch.

olivia: Thanks. Docs + support macros incoming. Tag me with edge cases (consolidated billing, prepaid orgs).
